prompt: `main.bicep` calls `modules/state.bicep`. What does the compiled `main.json` contain at its top level?
hint: Look at the first jq answer in this lesson.

choices.text: The three storage resources, flattened into one list
choices.why: They are inside, one level down, in the nested template.

choices.text: One nested deployment holding the module's template
choices.why: Right. A module compiles to a Microsoft.Resources/deployments resource.

choices.text: A link to the module file, fetched at deployment
choices.why: Local modules are embedded; nothing is fetched from your disk later.

choices.text: Nothing until the module is published to a registry
choices.why: A local path compiles in place; a registry is one option, not a requirement.

prompt: Two different modules in `main.bicep` are both given `name: 'storage'`. What goes wrong in the resource group?
hint: What does a module's name name?

choices.text: Both storage accounts get the same name
choices.why: Account names come from their own parameters, not from the module's name.

choices.text: Bicep refuses to compile duplicate module names
choices.why: The question is about what happens in Azure; the record is the problem.

choices.text: One deployment record overwrites the other
choices.why: Right. The name names a nested deployment, and two under one name share one record.

choices.text: The second module is skipped as a duplicate
choices.why: Nothing is skipped silently; the records collide.

prompt: Why does the shop build the account name with `uniqueString(resourceGroup().id)`?
hint: It must be the same every time, and unlikely to be taken.

choices.text: It changes on every deployment, so old accounts are never reused
choices.why: It is deterministic; a changing name would create a new account each time.

choices.text: Stable per group, and unlikely to clash worldwide
choices.why: Right. Storage account names are global, and the hash keeps the name fixed for the group.

choices.text: Azure requires it for every storage account
choices.why: It is a convention, not a requirement.

choices.text: It encrypts the name so it cannot be read in logs
choices.why: A hash is not encryption, and the name is not a secret.

prompt: `main.wrong.bicepparam` sets `environment = 'production'` and an undeclared `region`. What does `bicep build-params` do?
hint: Compare with the warning in lesson 4.

choices.text: Writes the file and warns about both
choices.why: Both are errors here, and no file was written.

choices.text: Ignores region and accepts production as a string
choices.why: That is how the old JSON parameter files behaved; the bicepparam file is checked.

choices.text: Refuses with two errors and exit status 1
choices.why: Right. The file names its template, so both mistakes are checked against it.

choices.text: Asks interactively for the right value
choices.why: It is a compiler; it reports and stops.

prompt: A colleague says `@secure()` means the password is safe everywhere. Using `db.parameters.json` from this lesson, what do you answer?

choices.text: It protects the value inside Azure; the generated file holds it in plain text
choices.why: Right. So a generated parameters file is never committed.

choices.text: Agreed: the generated file stores it encrypted
choices.why: The transcript shows the value in clear.

choices.text: It is safe in the file, but not in the deployment history
choices.why: The reverse: secure keeps it out of the history, and the file has it in clear.

choices.text: It is safe as long as the variable name is secret
choices.why: The name SHOP_DB_PASSWORD hides nothing; the value is the secret.

prompt: A `.bicepparam` file names the template it belongs to with the keyword ___.
Match each what-if change type to its meaning.

pairs.right: Not there yet, will be made
There, and some properties will change
There, not in the template, left alone
There, and what-if cannot tell what changes

right_distractors: Deleted because the file no longer names it

prompt: What-if shows Modify on `minimumTlsVersion` of the state account, a property nobody changed in the file. What is the likely story?

choices.text: What-if always lists every property
choices.why: It lists those that would change, plus some known noise.

choices.text: Somebody changed it by hand, and the deployment will undo that
choices.why: Right. Modify on an untouched property is drift, worth reading before deploying.

choices.text: The API version in the file is too old to set it
choices.why: An old API version would fail to compile or ignore it, not show a change.

choices.text: Bicep changed the value during compilation
choices.why: The compiled JSON carries what the file says.

prompt: The shop deletes a Redis cache from `main.bicep` and redeploys normally. What-if had listed it as Ignore. What is true a month later?
hint: What does incremental mode do to what it no longer sees?

choices.text: It was deleted at the redeploy
choices.why: Incremental deployments never delete what the file stops mentioning.

choices.text: Azure deleted it after 30 days without a deployment
choices.why: Nothing expires resources for lack of deployments.

choices.text: It was moved to a recycle bin
choices.why: No such thing happens to an ignored resource.

choices.text: It still runs, and is billed
choices.why: Right. Ignore means left alone, which is what a stack with deleteResources changes.

prompt: Which stack setting stops somebody deleting the shop's app service plan from the portal?

choices.text: --action-on-unmanage deleteResources
choices.why: That decides what happens to resources leaving the file.

choices.text: --deny-settings-mode denyDelete
choices.why: Right. Deletion by any route outside the stack is refused.

choices.text: --action-on-unmanage detachAll
choices.why: Detaching stops managing; it protects nothing.

choices.text: The stack's name
choices.why: A name protects nothing.

prompt: Why does the shop never use `deleteResources` on the resource group holding the Terraform state account?
hint: What would a careless edit of the file then delete?

choices.text: Stacks cannot manage storage accounts
choices.why: They can; the question is whether they should delete one.

choices.text: deleteResources is slower than detachAll
choices.why: Speed is not the concern.

choices.text: A line removed by mistake would delete the state, which lesson 7 is about
choices.why: Right. Where loss is unrecoverable, a deletion should never follow from an edit.

choices.text: Terraform refuses to use an account a stack manages
choices.why: Terraform does not know or care which tool created the account.

prompt: Put the shop's path for a change to main.bicep in order.
hint: Check locally, ask Azure, ask a person, then deploy.
items: bicep build and lint, with warnings failing the step
A person approves, reading the what-if
trap: Running what-if before the local checks is the slip: Azure would be asked about a file that does not even compile.

prompt: Which of these did this lesson run on your computer? Choose all that apply.
hint: Anything that needs the real resource group was read.

choices.text: Compiling a module into a nested deployment
choices.why: Yes. bicep build, locally.

choices.text: Refusing a value @allowed does not permit
choices.why: Yes. build-params checked it against the template.

choices.text: A what-if against rg-shop
choices.why: No. It needs Resource Manager and the real group.

choices.text: Creating a deployment stack with denyDelete
choices.why: No. A stack is a resource in a subscription.
